conditions.name: R&D expenditure
conditions.definition: Gross domestic expenditure on research and development as a share of GDP.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: money committed to research is what a country spends, and spending it does not show the country reads the future well (D122).

conditions.name: Researchers in R&D
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: a standing stock of people who could investigate is what a country has, not a record of what they found (D122). Correlates with income but survives size normalization.

conditions.name: Secure internet servers
conditions.definition: Servers using encryption in internet transactions, per million people.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: a diffusion stock of digital adoption that money buys, not an act of anticipation (D122). Spans four orders of magnitude, so its rank is read on the published value and its correlations on the logged one.

conditions.name: Individuals using the internet
conditions.definition: Share of the population that used the internet in the last three months.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: access to the basic tool of modern agency is what people have to act with, not a record of them acting (D122). Saturates near 95%, which compresses the top of the range.

conditions.name: Financial account ownership
conditions.definition: Adults with an account at a bank or mobile money provider.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: holding an account is the precondition for almost any economic action, not the action (D122). Global Findex, published every three years.

conditions.name: Credit to the private sector
conditions.definition: Domestic credit provided to the private sector by financial corporations.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: financial depth is a stock of money available to actors, not what they do with it (D122). High values can also signal a credit bubble, so more is not always better.

checks.name: Bribery incidence
checks.definition: Firms asked for at least one bribe payment across six public transactions covering utilities, permits, licences and taxes.
checks.note: Experience rather than reputation: the question asks whether the responding firm was itself asked, so it is not the perception composite D23 retired. It covers 50 of 53 countries and 45 of them at 2023 or later. It is not scored because it carries income. On a rank-normalised estimate it correlates with log GDP per capita at about 0.66 alone and takes the two-indicator Trust dimension to about 0.53, against 0.14 for contract enforcement days by itself, which is a larger wealth contribution than the one D44 retired an indicator over. Read it beside the score, not as the score.

conditions.name: Tertiary enrolment
conditions.definition: Gross enrolment ratio in tertiary education.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: enrolment counts people in formal education and records nothing learned (D122).

conditions.name: Public education expenditure
conditions.definition: Government expenditure on education as a share of GDP.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: public spending on education is a pure input, and learning is what the dimension asks about (D122).

indicators.name: Early-stage entrepreneurial activity
indicators.source: Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (APS key indicators, TEA rate)

indicators.name: Tolerance of entrepreneurial failure
indicators.source: Global Entrepreneurship Monitor (APS key indicators, fear of failure rate)

conditions.name: Fixed broadband subscriptions
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: installed infrastructure is what a country has to change with, not a record of it changing (D122). Penalizes mobile-first countries such as India and South Africa.

conditions.name: Output per worker
conditions.definition: GDP per person employed, constant purchasing power parity.
conditions.note: A condition, not scored: output per worker is income per worker, the wealth the benchmark tests capability against, so it is published beside Building as context (D122).

checks.name: Political polarization
checks.definition: Whether supporters of opposing political camps generally meet in a friendly or a hostile manner, rated by V-Dem country experts from 0, friendly, to 4, hostile.
checks.note: The question counts hostility and leaves disagreement alone, which is what pluralism asks for. It is not scored because a low reading has two causes the number cannot tell apart. Where camps compete openly, a calm reading means people who disagree still meet as fellow citizens. Where no opposition may organize, it means there is no camp left to be hostile to. In 2024 the five closed autocracies in the frame average 1.85 and the liberal democracies 1.77, while electoral democracies and electoral autocracies sit near 2.8 and 3.0. Scored, the reading would have lifted the United Arab Emirates and Rwanda about 11 points on this capability for a uniformity the benchmark does not count as shared purpose. Income is not why it is left out: richer countries read only somewhat calmer, at about -0.34 against log GDP per capita.
